findings.description: The cover title '海洋变暖与南极海冰骤减' is set far too large for the white card. Only '海洋变暖与南' fits inside the card. '极' runs past the card's right edge and is hidden behind the yellow 'Aa' circle, and the rest of the title ('…海冰骤减') runs off the right edge of the 1920-px frame, so it is clipped or hidden. The title should sit on one line inside the card. The other cover items are correct: the 中考英语 · 阅读理解 tag, 中考英语 2026年 北京 · 阅读C, 说明文 · 自然与环境, and 全文 348 词, which matches the reference count.

The font size on this screen is abnormal. The English sentence is about 1.5x the size used on the other screens: the cap height is about 80 px against about 55 px elsewhere. The first line, 'Some research¹ has', starts at y≈88, so its tops overlap the purple header band and the yellow rule under it. The Chinese translation is also oversized (about 70 px glyphs against about 42 px). Its second line, '升高。', runs into the footer and is drawn on top of 'SENTENCE 3 / 17', which can no longer be read, and its '。' sits on the start of the progress bar. The vocabulary panel itself is correct (1 research, 2 suggest, 3 air temperature, 4 cause) and so is the progress position.

The vocabulary panel is rendered at a hugely oversized font, with headwords about 60 px high, and its contents spill out of the card at both ends. At the top, entries 1–3 (researcher, input…into, recorded) are pushed above the panel: the tail of the recorded meaning, '记录下来的', overlaps the VOCABULARY tag, and a stray badge number '3' and an italic 'adj.' appear inside the purple header. The header text '2026年 北京 · 阅读C  海洋变暖与南极海冰骤减' is garbled or partly erased there (it reads something like '26 年 北京( 门 实( 海洋 变 暖 南极海冰骤减'). At the bottom, entry 8 'sea ice 海冰' crosses the panel's bottom border and overlaps the footer progress bar and knob. Entry 9 (grow) is cut off at the bottom edge of the frame.

Because of the overflow, the panel shows only entries 4 ocean, 5 data, 6 computer model, 7 project and 8 sea ice, plus a cut-off 9. The English carries badges 1–11: researchers¹, input…into², recorded³, ocean⁴, data⁵, computer model⁶, projected⁷, sea ice⁸, grow⁹, as¹⁰ and real world¹¹. Entries 1, 2, 3, 10 and 11 (researcher, input…into, recorded, as, real world) cannot be seen at all, and 9 is clipped, so the visible panel set does not match the badge set in the English.

In the Chinese translation the character '洲' of '南极洲' is missing and drawn as a dark boxed hex/notdef glyph, so the line reads '南极▯四周环绕着一条由强风和风暴构成的地带。' It should read '南极洲四周环绕着…'. The same character renders correctly in the panel entry 'Antarctica n. 南极洲' on this screen.

The first English line, 'These winds blow¹', starts at x≈610 instead of the left margin at x≈90, leaving a blank gap of about 520 px at the start of the line, as if it were right-aligned. The second line, 'surface water² and ice forward³.', starts at the normal left margin. Every other screen sets the English flush left, and this short sentence should start at the left margin. The numbering is correct (1 blow, 2 surface water, 3 forward; SENTENCE 11 / 17).

findings.description: The cover says "全文 259 词". Counting the reference English with the Chinese notes (建筑)/(设计)/(卢浮宫) removed gives 260 words. The extra word is in sentence 17, "his idea—let light design the buildings". The counter splits on whitespace (中考/阅读/passages.json words=259), so the closed-up em dash makes "idea—let" one word, but it is two words, idea and let. This is an off-by-one, and some counting conventions treat a closed em-dash pair as one word.

In the rounded English font, capital I is identical to lowercase l. Measured on screen 22, "It" I and "later" l are both 44–45 px tall plain stems. So the name "Ieoh Ming Pei" reads as "leoh Ming Pei", both in the English line and in the panel headword (entry 1). Students cannot guess the right letter from context in an unfamiliar proper name. "It" on screens 17, 22 and 24 has the same I/l ambiguity, but context makes those readable.

In "idea²—let", the purple badge 2 is about 1–2 px from the start of the em dash (pixel check at 1920 px). The badge looks attached to the dash with no clearance, which no other badge on these screens does.

findings.description: Vocabulary entry 1 'spend v. 度过；花（时间）' wraps between 花 and its qualifier, so line 1 ends '度过；花' and '（时间）' sits alone on line 2. This break falls at punctuation, so the wrap rule technically allows it; it is a typesetting-quality issue, not a rendering error.

verdicts.why: The wrap is there as described: screen12, entry 1 shows 'spend v. 度过；花' on line 1 and '（时间）' on line 2, flush with the headword. The text matches the reference ('v. 度过；花（时间）'). But the break falls before an opening bracket, which is a normal break point in Chinese typesetting. It also follows the intended rule that a vocabulary meaning wraps only at punctuation or between words. make_video.py's zh_html(gloss=True) deliberately cuts glosses into chunks before opening brackets, and FIT deliberately forces a line break before a bracket that lands at the start of a line. Nothing is clipped or overlapping, the leading bracket is flush, and the line stays readable. Breaking after '；' instead would be a style preference, not a defect, and the reporter itself says it is 'technically allowed'.

The wrap is there as described: screen13, entry 4 shows 'share v. 分享；讲述' on line 1 and '（想法、经历等）' on line 2. The text matches the reference ('v. 分享；讲述（想法、经历等）'). As with index 0, the break comes before an opening bracket, which is allowed in Chinese typesetting and follows the intended rule (wrap only at punctuation or between words). The renderer splits gloss chunks at opening brackets on purpose. Nothing is cut off or overlapping, the bracket is flush left, and the entry is readable. Keeping '讲述（想法、经历等）' together is a style preference, not a rendering defect.
